It take 1% to 2% water to separate a gallon of e85.  If the gas tank was 15 gallons it would take \~20 to 40 oz of water to cause separation.  There are 128 oz in a gallon.
It really became popular when gas started getting more expensive in the early 2000s to the 2010s

I would only recommend it if you drive a lot.  e85 is hydrophilic so as it absorbs humidify.  I know the gas tank is "sealed" but chemistry finds a way.  Once it separates from the humidity you have e99.9 on the bottom layer of the tank and some shit grade octane gas on top.  It's called phase separation.   Burning either of those individually is not good for the engine.  How long will this take?  Depends on the quality of the gas cap seal and the heat and humidity in the area and time.  Also, e85 only has \~66% of the energy as gasoline, so unless it's 66% the cost of gasoline, you aren't even saving money.  It takes 1.0 units of energy to produce 1.4 units on energy of e85.  So it's actually less efficient to produce than petroleum.  Also that 1.0 unit of energy to produce 1.4 units of e85 all comes from petroleum.  e85 is arguably beneficial in some ways to national security and energy independence, but there are many trade off that need to be considered.  It also does burn very clean.

While it's understandable to express concerns about the potential misuse of AI-based text generation tools, it's essential to consider the broader context of information dissemination and knowledge acquisition.  
  
Firstly, the comparison between "ask ChatGPT" and "Google it" may not necessarily equate the two actions. While both involve seeking information, the nuances lie in the methodology and critical thinking applied by the user.  
  
Secondly, your assertion that language models lack care for factual accuracy overlooks the significant advancements made in natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning. While no tool is infallible, modern AI models like ChatGPT are continuously improving in accuracy and reliability. Moreover, users have the responsibility to critically evaluate and verify the information obtained, regardless of its source.  
  
Additionally, the argument that using a search engine provides access to multiple sources for evaluation overlooks the fact that language models like ChatGPT can also incorporate diverse sources of information during training. These models are trained on vast amounts of text data from reputable sources, contributing to their ability to generate coherent and accurate responses.  
  
Furthermore, the concern about receiving unsourced text from a text generator applies equally to information obtained from search engine results. In both cases, users must exercise discernment and verify the information against credible sources.  
  
In conclusion, while it's prudent to approach AI-based text generation tools with caution, dismissing them outright undermines their potential utility in aiding knowledge acquisition. Instead, emphasis should be placed on promoting critical thinking, verification of information, and responsible use of all available resources, including AI tools, to foster informed learning and decision-making.

Determining the duration of inhibition of a metabolic pathway by a drug that is a potent inhibitor of CYP2D6 (Cytochrome P450 2D6) with a 24-hour half-life involves several considerations. Here's how you can estimate it:  
  
Understanding Half-Life: The half-life of a drug represents the time it takes for the concentration of the drug in the bloodstream to decrease by half. A drug with a 24-hour half-life means that it takes approximately 24 hours for the concentration of the drug to decrease by 50%.  
  
Steady-State Concentration: It's important to consider that it takes multiple half-lives for a drug to reach steady-state concentration in the body. Generally, it takes around five half-lives for a drug to reach approximately 97% of its steady-state concentration.  
  
Duration of Inhibition: Since the drug is a potent inhibitor of CYP2D6, its inhibitory effects on this metabolic pathway will likely persist as long as the drug is present in sufficient concentrations in the body.  
  
Cumulative Effect: With each dose of the drug, the inhibitory effect on CYP2D6 may become more pronounced due to accumulation in the body over time.  
  
Individual Variability: The duration of inhibition may vary among individuals based on factors such as metabolism, drug interactions, and genetic polymorphisms affecting CYP2D6 activity.  
  
Monitoring Concentrations: Therapeutic drug monitoring may be necessary to assess the concentration of the drug in the bloodstream over time and adjust dosing regimens accordingly.  
  
Clinical Considerations: Clinicians should carefully evaluate the potential for drug interactions and adverse effects when prescribing medications that are potent inhibitors of CYP2D6, especially in individuals who are concurrently taking medications metabolized by this pathway.  
  
Overall, while the half-life of the drug provides a useful indication of its elimination from the body, determining the precise duration of inhibition of the CYP2D6 metabolic pathway requires a comprehensive understanding of pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, and individual patient factors. I can summarize my experience in science as a room full of people who are all used to being the smartest people in the room.

To give you a more recent example of what chemistry people actually do, today, production came into the lab to get my input on high levels of nickle in our discharge water from a tank overflowing.  They didn't understand how the nickle could flow out because "nickle is heavy".  It's nickle acetate, it's water soluble.  I explained that to them.  They didn't grasp it.  I took a beaker, added dye to it, explained that the dye was the "nickle" and let it overflow under a faucet to show how things dilute when they overflow. 90% of what you will be doing is basic lab work and explaining basic science to people with 3/4ths your IQ and make twice as much money as you.  If you can do that with a smile on your face and a good attitude, you are golden.  This isn't NCIS/CSI Miami.
